relationships.subject: SARS-CoV-2
relationships.evidence_quote: SARS-CoV-2 attacks the organism by attaching itself to ACE2 via its spike protein, which allows its RNA to enter the healthy cell permitting the virus to replicate through a complex sequence of steps [6, 7].

relationships.subject: SARS-CoV-2
relationships.evidence_quote: CD147 (also known as basigin) has been implicated as another receptor to which the SAR-CoV-2 spike protein is capable of binding, thus serving as an additional route of brain infection [26].

relationships.subject: ACE2
relationships.evidence_quote: It has been suggested that ACE2 may influence GABA (gamma-aminobutyric acid) neurotransmission in the amygdala and possibly elsewhere in the brain, pointing to another possible target of the virus [15].

key_findings: SARS-CoV-2 may reach the brain via olfactory axonal transport or a hematogenous route, with ACE2 expressed in neurons and glia.
Neurological symptoms are common in COVID-19 and associated with greater disease severity.
